description: Barina distributes work across supercomputers in units of 2^40 consecutive integers (~10s on GPU). Angeltveit shards by residue class (55 to 278699 cases of similar runtime). Both face distributed computing challenges of fault tolerance and progress tracking.
mathematical_formalization: Barina: partition [1, 2^N] into intervals [i*2^40, (i+1)*2^40). Angeltveit: partition by residue classes mod 2^k, yielding C(k) cases. Load balance: Var(T_i) / E[T_i]^2 measures uniformity.
analogical_connections: MapReduce shuffling — partition by key for balanced loads
BOINC volunteer computing — distribute independent work units with checkpointing
implementation_hypothesis: Work-unit server tracks completion status. For Angeltveit sharding, precompute ~278699 cases on coordinator, assign batches to GPU workers. Workers report checksums. Coordinator validates against CPU reference sample.
experiment_seed: Simulate both sharding strategies for N=72 with heterogeneous GPU fleet. Measure makespan, load imbalance, network overhead.
